    What city is Purdue University in?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    Purdue University's main campus is located in West Lafayette, Indiana, part of the twin cities area of Lafayette-West Lafayette, situated along the Wabash River. The university also has other locations, including Purdue University in Indianapolis and Purdue University Global, but West Lafayette is its primary home.
     
    • West Lafayette, IN: The main campus, near I-65, about an hour north of Indianapolis and two hours south of Chicago. 
    • Lafayette, IN: The neighboring city, forming the Lafayette-West Lafayette metropolitan area. 
    • Indianapolis, IN: A significant Purdue University extension campus.

      Why is Purdue so famous?
      An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
      AI Overview
      Purdue University is famous for its elite STEM programs, particularly engineering, producing numerous astronauts and Nobel laureates, alongside strong business and health sciences, all while maintaining affordability through tuition freezes and strong industry ties. Its reputation is built on rigorous academics, high research output (R1 status), an impactful alumni network, and a focus on practical, experiential learning, making it a globally recognized leader in innovation. 
      Key Reasons for Fame:
      • STEM Excellence: World-renowned for engineering, with top-tier rankings and producing figures like Neil Armstrong; also strong in computer science, pharmacy, and nursing. 
      • Innovation & Research: Classified as an "R1: Doctoral University – Very high research activity," with extensive research labs, centers, and significant patent activity. 
      • Affordability & Value: Known for fiscal responsibility, including multi-year tuition freezes, providing high-value education without excessive cost. 
      • Impactful Alumni: Boasts a powerful alumni network, including 27 astronauts, Nobel laureates, and leaders in various fields, fostering strong career opportunities. 
      • Experiential Learning: Offers extensive co-ops, internships, and research opportunities, connecting students directly to real-world experience. 
      • Strong Reputation: Consistently ranks among top public universities globally, known for academic rigor and practical outcomes. 
      In essence, Purdue's fame stems from its blend of cutting-edge academic programs, commitment to affordability, vast research contributions, and powerful industry and alumni connections, all contributing to its status as a leading global university.

        Is a 3.7 GPA good for Purdue?
        An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
        AI Overview
        Yes, a 3.7 GPA is generally considered very good for Purdue, placing you within or above the typical range for admitted students, especially if it's unweighted or you've taken challenging courses, though admission competitiveness varies by college (e.g., Engineering is tougher). Most admitted students fall between 3.7-4.0, but strong essays, extracurriculars, and good test scores can strengthen your application significantly. 
        Purdue GPA Profile
        • Overall Middle 50% GPA: 3.70-4.00, with averages often around 3.7-3.8, making it strongly competitive. 
        • A mix of A's and B's: You'll need more A's than B's, and AP/IB classes help. 
        Factors that Boost Your Application
        • Challenging Coursework: Taking AP, IB, or other honors classes shows college readiness and boosts weighted GPAs. 
        • Strong Essays: A compelling personal essay is crucial to stand out.
        • Extracurriculars: Leadership, internships, and community service help. 
        • Strong Test Scores: If below average for your major, high SAT/ACT scores can compensate. 
        Major-Specific Considerations
        • High-Demand Programs: Colleges like Engineering and Computer Science are more competitive and may require higher GPAs (e.g., First-Year Engineering average is closer to 3.9).
        • Less Competitive Programs: A 3.7 is even stronger for less impacted majors or other Purdue colleges.
        In short: A 3.7 GPA is a solid foundation for Purdue, but its strength depends on your major, coursework rigor, and the overall strength of your complete application.

          Mascot: Purdue Pete, Boilermaker Special
          Typical SAT scores: Reading and Writing 600-720, Math 600-760 (2023–24) IPEDS
          Students: 57,876 (fall 2025)
          Nickname: Boilermakers
